Jordan / team — quick technical notes to seed the kickoff so we can keep the meeting focused: (see attached redwood-sample-mapping.json)

SCIM specifics (Redwood Private CP):
- We implement SCIM 2.0 (push provisioning). Minimum supported attributes we require to map identities: userName, id (externalId), name.givenName, name.familyName, emails[type=work], active. Groups must be provided as SCIM Group resources with members referencing user ids.
- Group sync cadence: we recommend immediate push for changes + nightly full reconciliation. Our staging token supports scoped, short-lived credentials for provisioning.
- Error handling: we surface per-user provisioning errors with 400/409 codes and a reconciliation report in the staging UI.

SAML attribute mapping / role binding:
- Supported assertion attributes: email, email_verified, given_name, family_name, and a custom attribute to carry role info. We recommend using an attribute name: https://redwood-inference.com/claims/roles or redwood_role (both supported).
- Mapping model: group -> role mapping via SCIM group sync is preferred. If you need direct role assertions from SAML we can accept a comma-separated role claim, but we require that role values match an agreed enumeration.
- Fallback / manual: we expose an admin UI to create manual user->role bindings if group sync fails during cutover.

Service accounts / machine identities:
- Create dedicated SCIM service accounts for CI/CD or automation. These are represented as users with externalId and an attribute service_account=true. Tokens for these accounts are long-lived but can be rotated via our API.

Security notes:
- We will only accept SAML metadata signed with an RSA key >= 2048 bits.
- SCIM provisioning endpoints are restricted to your VPC egress IP list; we'll provide a short token exchange flow and recommend rotating tokens every 90 days.

I'll attach a sample mapping JSON for your team to review. We'll go over mapping choices during the call to validate edge cases (contractors, vendors, ephemeral accounts).
